why: Rule 1/2: the 290 cm muon carries a 2.5 cm 195k e/cm proton stub at ~90 deg only at this low-z end (z=263 vs 477), the only nearby small clusters sit here, and the far end 14003/14000 is a single stopping end split by a fit break rather than a second Bragg.
Rule 1: the 8 cm proton rises monotonically away from here to its Bragg peak at 11001 while the 21 cm MIP muon leaves the other way across a 138 deg kink.
Rule 1: the contained 234 cm muon shows its stopping-muon Bragg shape at 9000 and cools toward 9001, which is also the lowest-z end and has two small blobs beside it.
Rule 1: degree-4 junction with four prongs at wide angles, a hot 6.5 cm proton stub and a 1.6 cm 150k stub, and no segment rising toward it; 8002 is a 167 deg collinear kink.
Rules 1 and 3: three prongs at a wide V, the 4.4 cm proton rises away, and the 56 cm pi+ has a textbook Bragg at 8005 followed by a mu-then-e decay chain, so 8005 is the far end.
Rule 1: degree-4 star where the 21 cm proton rises monotonically 65k to 250k away toward 13010 and the 59 cm muon also Braggs away at 13007.
Rule 8 territory with only 3.5 cm of charge in the whole event; the 2 cm proton blob is the only object that can host a vertex and it is cooler at 3001 than at 3000.

Rule 7 locates the junction confidently - a 35 cm track meets the shower apex across a 51 deg kink - but 17000 and 60026 straddle it 1.9 cm apart and only the shower back-extrapolation (1.3 cm to 17000 vs 1.9 cm the other way) breaks the tie, so the id is close to a coin flip.
Rule 1: a three-prong proton star with every prong hotter away from it, and the 125 cm muon lines up straight back through the blobs 84029 and 85031 to this same point.
Rules 1 and 2: the 152 cm muon has its sharp 215k Bragg spike at 3000 so it starts at 3001, which is the lower-z end and has the whole cloud of small debris blobs downstream of it.
Rule 1: degree-3 vertex where the 5.9 cm proton rises 165k to 204k away toward 9006, the 165 cm muon Braggs away at 9000, and an EM bush hangs off the third prong.
Rule 1 in its cleanest form: both attached segments rise away at a 65 deg V, the 16 cm proton reaching 212k at 15004 and the 115 cm muon running out to the y wall.
Rule 1: degree-3 junction where all three prongs (111 cm muon, 13 cm proton to 174k, 18 cm pi+) get hotter going away from it.

Hot-blob trap: the 62 cm track is flat MIP and only spikes in the final 1.5 cm, so that is vertex charge and not a Bragg rise; the 3.6 cm 128k proton stub leaves at 118 deg (a real prong, not a mis-split Bragg tail) and the debris cloud sits at this lower-z end.
Rule 1: three of three prongs rise away from this lowest-z vertex, with the 10.8 cm pi+ Bragging to 188k at 6005.
